svg.title: For example the first A entry is P3 k=0 ∂0Q0k,0k;01,01(e0)/ν2 = −256; the corresponding B entry is the same sum over ordered i, k ̸= 0, which is zero. For C sum ∂rQrk,0k;01,01 over r ̸= 0, k. The other row uses 12, 12. These finite sums and (FC6) give respectively the three displayed columns. A third, undifferentiated sample correlates tensor component 01 at e0 with Q02,12 at zero; its columns are (0, 0, −16), directly from (FC5). It separates the last tensor direction. Thus A, B, C are independent, so the tensor space has dimension exactly three. The two divergence samples in (FC7) are independent; combined with the upper bound two from (FC4), they identify the entire polar vector space and prove surjectivity of divergence. Rank-nullity gives a one-dimensional conserved kernel. Solving (FC7) yields its generator
